## My request:
never mind about the S3 upload, I am back at my laptop.
the aesthetic I was thinking for the quote was more like the images i attached.

I think the gallop/hoove beat needs to be stronger/more punchy/more base-y. I know that might not be what it might actually sound like in this terrain, but still prefer punchiness. Oh I notice that you did mentioned addressing "hoof weight" next, I guess you probably meant the same thing
I am not sure about the narration starting immediately as the sequence opens. I think we need to give a second or two for the horse beat and music to register with the audience, and then the narration kicks-in. 
You are gonna have to buy another second or two somewhere. Make a call on that, just not the final shot after the turn, that is long enough already. In fact I want you to think critically of this narration bit, and give me an honest opinion about if this works. it sounds weird to me right now, bit of a disconnect between the fast paced action vs the calm collected almost documentary like narration of the brit officer. but I am also guessing that's where our music is going to come in.
Other than that, this is good. the "pathan" pronunciation now sounds right.

give me you recommendations first.

before you finalize the narration, I recommend you check out the music. The officer's voice is also going to contrast significantly with the larger than life music and all of this needs to come together
